- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.8) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low or neutral (0.0–0.4) — model is overly optimistic in such periods.
- Lagged mean reversion: if recent 3–5 days show downward trend, forecast should not continue upward unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — model often overweights sentiment without sufficient historical context.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 7–10 days) — adjust downward if sentiment is cooling.
- If sentiment is consistently high (>0.7) over 3–5 days, model should not forecast sharp declines — expect mean reversion, not reversal.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6), model often overfits recent volatility — use smoother trend filters.
- Forecast should not exceed 1.5x the 14-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.85).
